sources.note: Nothing. The source of Ethnologue's Amravati-district Bhalay entry: Bhalays 'comprise up to 40 percent of the population of some villages' in Amravati dt; wordlists 'collected from the Bhalays, the Gowlans, the Korkus, and the Gonds living in Chikli' (Appendix, p. c.1209 of text) but no Bhalay wordlist or similarity table is published; sec. 7.2.5: 'The language of the Bhalay community also needs further investigation including their understanding of the regional languages.'

Pop. 8,670 (1981 census); Maharashtra, Amravati District; 'Lexical similarity 90% with Gowlan [goj]'; 'Indo-Aryan, Southern zone, Unclassified'; 'Bhalay probably an alternate spelling of Balahi (Balai), a Scheduled Caste found in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh.'

sources.citation: Lekhwani, Kanhaiyalal. 1979. Descriptive analysis of Nimadi. PhD thesis, University of Poona (Deccan College). Shodhganga hdl 10603/145363. (already held under nima1243)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Nimadi (nima1243), not 'Bhalay'; no mention of Balahi speech. Sec. 2.6.3 pp. 89-92: one heavy stress per phonological word, not phonemic at word level, position by vowel length/syllable structure (rules i-xiii). Already the catalog statement for nima1243.

sources.citation: Hans, Krishnalal. 1960. Nimāṛī aur uskā sāhitya. Allahabad: Hindustani Academy. (Hindi; already held under nima1243)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Balahi stress specifically; §97 (running head 'Nimāṛī bhāṣā', c. p.66): the Balahi are c. 8% of the Nimar population, divided into Nimāṛī Balāhī and Katiyā, and 'both groups of Balahi speak a Nimadi on which a combined influence of Bhili, Malvi and Khandeshi is seen'. Its Nimadi word-stress section (§312-314, p.121) is recorded under nima1243.

sources.citation: Fuchs, Stephen. 1950. The Children of Hari: A Study of the Nimar Balahis in the Central Provinces of India (Wiener Beiträge zur Kulturgeschichte und Linguistik 8). Vienna: Herold. (archive.org IGNCA scan, scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. pp. 8-9 (identity only): 'the Balahis have no language of their own. In the Nimar they commonly speak the Nimari dialect which is a form of the Malvi dialect of Rajasthani.. It is said of the Balahis that they, more than other castes of the district, mix many Marathi words into their speech, and also that they have a broader and coarser way of pronunciation.. in the village and among themselves the Balahis speak Nimari.'

sources.citation: Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank. Glottolog 5.3, languoid bhal1245 'Bhalay' (Bookkeeping), retirement note citing Russell & Hiralal 1916:106.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States: 'Bhalay [bhx] is listed in E16-E28 as a separate language. However, Bhalay is a caste rather than an ethnic group with a particular language, and if they speak a language separate from their neighbours, it is Nimadi [noe]'. Zero descriptive references (only Koppers 1942 overview, Russell & Hiralal 1916 ethnographic).

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. & Hira Lal. 1916. The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, vol. II, article 'Balahi', pp. 105-108. London: Macmillan. (archive.org scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnography only; p.106 on the subcastes: 'Nimari is a local subdivision indicating those who speak the peculiar dialect of this tract' (i.e. Nimari/Nimadi). This is the page Glottolog cites for the retirement.
